package_info.why_malicious: This package is a typosquatted clone of a legitimate npm package, differing by a single character in the name. It delivers the r77 rootkit, a known malicious payload, to infected systems, enabling stealthy persistence and unauthorized access.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code executes an install.js script, which downloads and installs the r77 rootkit, granting the attacker stealthy access to the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing additional scripts during postinstall is a common technique for malware delivery, especially when the script downloads and installs rootkits.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not download or install rootkits or perform privileged system modifications during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may run postinstall scripts to compile native modules or set up dependencies, but not to install rootkits.
key_indicators: Typosquatted package name mimicking a popular library
Postinstall script that downloads and executes external binaries

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a malicious executable (r77.exe) from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, resulting in rootkit installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing binaries from untrusted remote sources is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not fetch and execute remote binaries, especially rootkits.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some developer tools may update themselves, but this is not expected in a utility package.
key_indicators: Hardcoded external URL for binary download

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (node-hide-console-windows), believing it to be legitimate.
install.js downloads r77 rootkit from a remote server and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Rootkit installed, attacker gains stealthy access

behavioral_signatures: npm package with postinstall script that downloads and executes external binaries
Typosquatted package names mimicking popular libraries
Runtime download and execution of Windows executables
file_indicators: Presence of install.js with network and process execution logic
Downloaded binary named r77.exe in C:\Windows\Temp
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests to untrusted or newly registered domains
Download of r77.exe or similar payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that download and execute binaries. Flag packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting). Detect outbound network requests to suspicious domains during or immediately after package installation. Look for the presence of known rootkit binaries (e.g., r77.exe) in temporary or system directories.
